Coordinate and execute ongoing infrastructure operations, management, and maintenance. Manage incident responses and ensure rapid restoration of services that fail. Proactively research and recommend courses of action to prevent problems and to maintain high infrastructure service levels for the user community. review_candidates.company: Global Green Energy & Power Corporation Limited
review_candidates.description: About the Role Global Green Energy & Power Corporation Limited (GGEP) is a London-headquartered renewable energy developer building a portfolio of utility-scale solar PV, battery storage and associated grid infrastructure across West Africa and other emerging markets. We are seeking an exceptional Head of Project Management to own the end-to-end delivery of large-scale solar PV projects upwards of 50 MW. GGEP, through its wholly owned subsidiary, is in the process to setup a 138.9 MW DC (110 MW AC) Solar PV project in Nimba County, Republic of Liberia. This is a hands-on leadership role for an engineer-manager who can move fluently between the technical design layer (energy yield simulation, plant layout, interconnection design) and the delivery layer (feasibility, procurement, EPC oversight, commissioning). The successful candidate will be based at our London global headquarters and will travel extensively across Africa to lead project sites and stakeholder engagement on the ground. 1 Core Technical Mandate This role is design-led. Beyond programme management, the candidate must personally direct, review and challenge the engineering basis of each plant. The following technical competencies are central to the role: 1.1 Energy Yield Simulation & Plant Designn • PVsyst — MANDATORY. Demonstrable, hands-on expertise in building and interrogating PVsyst models is an essential, non-negotiable requirement. The candidate must be able to construct simulations from scratch, define near/far shading scenes, configure module and inverter databases, set loss parameters (soiling, temperature, mismatch, DC/AC ohmic, availability), and critically review P50/P90 energy yield outputs to validate or contest a developer's or EPC's bankable production estimates. • PVcase — DESIRABLE (not mandatory). Working experience with PVcase (or comparable AutoCAD-based / terrain-aware layout tools) for rapid site layout optimisation, row spacing, ground-coverage-ratio studies and cut-and-fill earthworks estimation is a strong advantage and will be viewed favourably. • Supporting tools. Familiarity with Helioscope, PlantPredict, AutoCAD, GIS/QGIS, and meteorological datasets (Meteonorm, SolarGIS, NSRDB) for resource assessment is beneficial. 1.2 Transmission & Grid Interconnection A strong, practical understanding of the transmission infrastructure that connects a solar PV plant to the grid is essential. The candidate is expected to own the interconnection workstream and be conversant with : • Point-of-interconnection (POI) selection, switchyard and substation scope, and the boundary between the developer's and the utility's assets. • HV/MV design fundamentals — step-up transformers, collector systems, MV/HV switchgear, protection and metering, and the associated single-line diagrams. • Overhead transmission line routing and design considerations for evacuating power to the national grid (e.g. regional networks such as the TRANSCO CLSG interconnector and national utilities across West Africa). • Grid code compliance, connection studies (load flow, fault level, reactive power/power factor, harmonics), grid impact assessments and the negotiation of connection/transmission agreements with system operators. • Curtailment, evacuation capacity constraints and the implications for plant sizing and revenue. 1.3 Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) Experience with battery energy storage projects is require d as GGEP increasingly pairs solar generation with storage to firm output, provide ancillary services and manage evacuation constraints. The candidate should understand: • BESS sizing and use-case definition — energy shifting, peak shaving, capacity firming, frequency response and grid-stability services. • Core technology and architecture — Li-ion chemistries (LFP vs NMC), DC- vs AC-coupled configurations, PCS/inverters, EMS/BMS, round-trip efficiency and degradation/augmentation planning. • Integration of solar-plus-storage at the design, controls and interconnection levels, and the safety, fire and standards regime (e.g. UL 9540 / 9540A, IEC, NFPA 855). • The commercial and dispatch logic that links BESS to the PPA, grid code and ancillary-service markets. 2. Key Responsibilities 2.1 Strategic Leadership • Develop and implement project management strategies for solar PV installations exceeding 50 MW, including paired BESS and grid-evacuation infrastructure. • Align project objectives with GGEP's mission to deliver sustainable, bankable energy solutions across its target markets. • Set the technical and delivery standards (design basis, gate reviews, quality benchmarks) applied across the portfolio. 2.2 Project Planning & Execution • Oversee the end-to-end project lifecycle — feasibility studies, energy yield modelling, design, permitting, procurement, construction and commissioning. • Manage multiple concurrent projects across several African countries, ensuring adherence to timelines, budgets and quality standards. • Own the project schedule (Primavera P6 / MS Project), critical path, cost control and the EPC/owner's-engineer interface through to commercial operation date (COD). • Lead technical due diligence and respond to lenders' independent engineers during bankability review. 2.3 Stakeholder Management • Build and maintain strong relationships with local authorities, utilities, system operators, regulators, contractors and community stakeholders. • Act as the primary point of contact for clients, partners, lenders and government counterparts during project execution. 2.4 Team Management • Lead and mentor a multidisciplinary project management team spanning engineering, procurement, construction and HSE. • Foster a culture of accountability, innovation, technical rigour and excellence. 2.5 Compliance & Risk Management • Ensure compliance with local regulations, grid codes, environmental and social standards (incl. IFC Performance Standards / Equator Principles where applicable) and organisational policies. • Identify, quantify and proactively mitigate project risks across technical, schedule, cost, regulatory and HSE dimensions; maintain the project risk register. 2.6 Travel & Mobility • Base: Monrovia, Republic of Liberia • Travel extensively across Africa to oversee project sites, supervise EPC delivery and lead stakeholder engagement, with the cadence driven by the construction programme. 3. Qualifications & Experience 3.1 Educational Background • Essential: Bachelor's degree in Electrical / Electronics / Energy / Mechanical Engineering, Renewable Energy or a related field. • Advantageous: MBA or equivalent advanced degree in Management. 3.2 Experience • Minimum 7–10 years of project management experience, with at least 5 years on large-scale solar PV projects (>50 MW). • Proven track record of delivering multi-million-dollar renewable energy projects in international settings; experience in Africa is strongly preferred. • Hands-on PVsyst modelling experience is mandatory and will be tested at interview. • Demonstrated experience taking utility-scale solar (ideally solar-plus-storage) from feasibility through to commissioning and COD. • Experience interfacing with utilities / system operators on grid connection and transmission infrastructure for a generation asset. 3.3 Skills & utilities/system • PVsyst — expert (mandatory). Independent model build, loss configuration and P50/P90 yield validation. • PVcase / layout tools — proficient (desirable). Terrain-aware layout and earthworks optimisation. • Transmission & grid interconnection literacy — substations, HV/MV design, grid code and connection studies. • BESS project understanding — sizing, technology, integration and standards. • Strong leadership and organisational skills; able to lead multidisciplinary teams in challenging environments. • Expertise in project planning tools — Primavera P6, MS Project or equivalent. • Excellent communication and negotiation skills; comfortable in front of lenders, regulators and government. • Cultural sensitivity and adaptability to diverse, frontier-market working environments. 3.4 Certifications • Advantageous: PMP (Project Management Professional) or equivalent project-management certification.
